title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
description: Learn practical security foundations, secure application patterns, and incident readiness for modern systems.

paths.title: Security Foundations
paths.description: Learn assets, threats, vulnerabilities, risk, and defense in depth.

paths.title: Secure Applications
paths.description: Protect identity, input, sessions, secrets, and dependencies.

paths.title: Incident Readiness
paths.description: Prepare logs, backups, response steps, and recovery.

cards.title: Security protects confidentiality, integrity, and availability
cards.prompt: Confidentiality limits unauthorized disclosure, integrity prevents unauthorized change, and availability keeps systems usable.
cards.content: A control can improve one goal while harming another, so security decisions should consider the complete service and its users.

cards.title: Risk combines likelihood and impact
cards.prompt: A vulnerability is a weakness; a threat is something capable of exploiting it; risk considers the resulting likelihood and harm.
cards.content: Prioritize risks using business context rather than fixing findings only by scanner severity.

cards.title: Recognize phishing
cards.prompt: Which message is the strongest phishing warning sign?

options: A routine internal notice with no links
An urgent request to sign in through an unfamiliar domain
A calendar invitation from a known colleague
question.explanation: Urgency plus an unfamiliar sign-in domain is a common credential-stealing pattern.

cards.title: Apply defense in depth
cards.prompt: Do not rely on one control to stop every failure.
cards.content: Layered controls reduce the chance that one mistake or bypass becomes a complete compromise.
items: Encrypt data in transit and at rest.

cards.title: Authentication proves identity; authorization checks permission
cards.prompt: Both checks belong on the trusted server for every protected action.
cards.content: Hiding a button in the frontend is not authorization because an attacker can call the underlying endpoint directly.

cards.title: All external input is untrusted
cards.prompt: Input can arrive through forms, APIs, files, headers, URLs, queues, and imported datasets.
cards.content: Validate shape and bounds, encode output for its context, and use safe APIs such as parameterized queries.

cards.title: Protect session cookies
cards.prompt: Which cookie configuration best protects a production session token?

options: Readable by JavaScript and sent over HTTP
HttpOnly, Secure, and an appropriate SameSite value
Stored in a URL query string
question.explanation: These attributes reduce script access, require HTTPS, and limit cross-site sending.

cards.title: Manage application secrets
cards.prompt: Secrets must be protected through their complete lifecycle.
cards.content: A secret accidentally committed to Git should be revoked and rotated; deleting the latest file does not remove it from history.
items: Store secrets in a managed secret system.
Never include secrets in browser bundles.
Restrict access by environment and role.
Rotate secrets regularly and after exposure.

cards.title: Logs are evidence for detection and response
cards.prompt: Security logs should reveal important identity, permission, configuration, and data-access events.
cards.content: Log enough context to investigate without storing passwords, complete tokens, or unnecessary personal data.

cards.title: Respond to a suspected incident
cards.prompt: Use a documented process so urgent decisions do not depend on memory.
cards.content: Preserve evidence and communicate carefully. Premature cleanup can destroy information needed to understand scope.

cards.title: A backup is only proven after restoration
cards.prompt: Backups can be incomplete, corrupted, inaccessible, or encrypted by the same attacker.
cards.content: Keep protected copies, define recovery objectives, and regularly test restoring the actual services and data.

cards.title: Security release gate
cards.prompt: Use a risk-based review before exposing a service to users.
cards.content: High-risk findings should block release or receive a documented exception with an owner and deadline.
